title: EU approves a 90 billion euro loan for Ukraine and adopts its 20th sanctions package
body:
On 23 April 2026, the European Union approved a loan package of 90 billion euros for Ukraine covering 2026 and 2027, according to RBC-Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and European Council President Antonio Costa both confirmed the decision. Zelensky said the loan had been unblocked and that the money would go to domestic weapons production, purchases of weapons Ukraine does not make itself, energy and winter preparedness, and social obligations. Costa also said that the 20th sanctions package against Russia was adopted the same day, writing: "Promised, delivered, implemented."

EU ambassadors had tentatively agreed on the loan and the sanctions package on 22 April. Hungary had blocked the funds for months over the suspension of oil supplies through the Druzhba pipeline and lifted its veto after transit resumed. Russian oil flows resumed in Slovakia on the night of 23 April, for the first time in nearly three months, and this was described as the key condition for Hungary and Slovakia lifting their vetoes. The first tranche of the loan could arrive in May or June 2026.
